The term '''resurgent function''' (from {{Langx|la|resurgere}}, to get up again) comes from French mathematician [[Jean Écalle]]'s ''theory of resurgent functions and alien calculus''. The theory evolved from the summability of divergent series (see [[Borel summation]]) and treats [[analytic function]]s with [[isolated singularity|isolated singularities]]. He introduced the term in the late 1970s.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/alien-calculus-could-save-particle-physics-from-infinities-20230406/|title=How to Tame the Endless Infinities Hiding in the Heart of Particle Physics|last=Wood|first=Charlie|website=Quanta Magazine|date=6 April 2023 |access-date=2023-08-27}}</ref>

''Resurgent functions'' have applications in [[asymptotic analysis]], in the theory of [[differential equations]], in [[perturbation theory]] and in [[quantum field theory]].

For analytic functions with isolated singularities, the '''Alien calculus''' can be derived, a special algebra for their derivatives.

== Definition ==
A '''<math>\Omega</math>-resurgent function''' is an element of <math>\mathbb{C}\delta\oplus \hat{\mathcal{R}}_{\Omega}</math>, i.e. an element of the form <math>c\delta + \hat{\phi}</math> from <math>\mathbb{C}\delta \oplus \mathbb{C}\{\zeta\}</math>, where <math>c\in \mathbb{C}</math> and <math>\hat{\phi}</math> is a ''<math>\Omega</math>-continuable [[germ (mathematics)|germ]]''.<ref name=DSR>{{cite book | author=Claude Mitschi, David Sauzin | title=Divergent Series, Summability and Resurgence I | language=en| edition=1| publisher=Springer Verlag | place=Switzerland| year=2016| ISBN= 9783319287355}}</ref>

A power series <math>\widetilde{\phi}\in \mathbb{C}[[z^{-1}]]</math> whose formal Borel transformation is a <math>\Omega</math>-resurgent function is called '''<math>\Omega</math>-resurgent series'''.

== Basic concepts and notation ==

'''Convergence at <math>\infty</math>:'''

The formal power series <math>\phi(z) \in \mathbb{C}[[z^{-1}]]</math> is ''convergent at <math>\infty</math>'' if the associated formal power series <math>\psi(t) = \phi(1/t) \in \mathbb{C}[[t]]</math> has a positive radius of convergence. <math>\mathbb{C}\{z^{-1}\}</math> denotes the space of ''formal power series convergent at <math>\infty</math>''.<ref name= DSR></ref>

'''Formal Borel transform:'''

The ''formal Borel transform'' (named after [[Émile Borel]]) is the operator <math>\mathcal{B}:z^{-1}\mathbb{C}[[z^{-1} ]]\to \mathbb{C}[[\zeta]]</math> defined by
:<math>\mathcal{B}:\phi=\sum\limits_{n=0}^\infty a_n z^{-n-1}\mapsto \hat{\phi }=\sum\limits_{n= 0}^\infty a_n \frac{\zeta^n}{n!}</math>.<ref name=DSR></ref>

'''Convolution in <math>\mathbb{C}\{\zeta\}</math>:'''

Let <math>\hat{\phi},\hat{\psi}\in \mathbb{C}[[\zeta]]</math>, then the [[convolution]] is given by
:<math>\hat{\phi}*\hat{\psi}:=\mathcal{B}[\phi\psi]</math>.

By adjunction we can add a [[unit (mathematics)|unit]] to the convolution in <math>\mathbb{C}[[\zeta]]</math> and introduce the vector space <math>\mathbb{C}\times \mathbb{C}[[z]]</math>, where we denote the <math>(1,0)</math> element with <math>\delta</math>. Using the convention <math>\{0\}\times \mathbb{C}[[\zeta]]:=\mathbb{C}[[\zeta]]</math> we can write the space as <math>\mathbb{C}\delta\oplus \mathbb{C}[[z]]</math> and define
:<math>(a\delta + \hat{\phi })*(b\delta + \hat{\psi }) := ab\delta + a\hat{\psi } + b \hat{\phi } +\hat{\phi}*\hat{\psi}</math>
and set <math>\mathcal{B}1 := \delta</math>.<ref name=DSR></ref>

'''<math>\Omega</math>-resummable seed:'''

Let <math>\Omega</math> be a non-empty [[discrete set|discrete]] subset of <math>\mathbb{C}</math> and define <math>\mathbb{D}_R=\{\zeta\in \mathbb{C}\mid |\zeta-0| < R\}\setminus\{0\}</math>.

Let <math>r</math> be the radius of convergence of <math>\hat{\phi}</math>. <math>\hat{\phi}</math> is a ''<math>\Omega</math>-continuable seed'' if an <math>R</math> exists such that <math>r \geq R>0</math> and <math>\mathbb{D}_R\cap \Omega=\emptyset</math>, and <math>\hat{\phi}</math> [[analytic continuation]] along some path in <math>\mathbb{C}\setminus \Omega</math> starting at a point in <math>\mathbb{D}_R</math>.

<math>\hat{\mathcal{R}}_{\Omega}</math> denotes the space of <math>\Omega</math>-continuable germs in <math>\mathbb{C}\{\zeta \}</math>.<ref name=DSR></ref>
